summary: LLM inference costs scale directly with tokens processed, so optimizing prompts, caching, and model selection can cut API spend by 50-90% while often improving latency. Teams commonly reduce monthly bills from $10K to $2K through a combination of prompt caching (up to 90% input savings), semantic caching (60-70% hit rates), and model cascading. Most high-impact techniques are low-effort and provider-agnostic, making optimization a near-immediate ROI investment.

techniques.name: Prompt Caching
techniques.description: Reuse cached prefixes of repeated prompts (system instructions, few-shot examples, long context) so the provider charges a steeply discounted rate for the cached portion on subsequent calls. It is the highest-leverage, lowest-risk cost reduction available in production.
techniques.savings: Up to 90% reduction on cached input tokens
techniques.example: Place your static 2,000-token system prompt and few-shot examples at the start of every request so Anthropic/OpenAI charge ~10% for those cached tokens on repeat calls within the cache TTL.

techniques.name: Semantic Caching
techniques.description: Cache responses keyed by the semantic meaning (embedding similarity) of a query rather than exact string match, returning stored answers for paraphrased or similar questions without hitting the LLM at all.
techniques.example: Use Redis semantic cache or GPTCache to return the stored answer when a new user query embeds within 0.95 cosine similarity of a previously answered question, skipping the LLM call entirely.

techniques.name: Model Cascading / Routing
techniques.description: Route simple or low-risk queries to small cheap models and escalate only hard queries to large expensive models, often verifying cheap-model confidence before falling back.
techniques.example: Send all requests first to GPT-4o-mini and only escalate to GPT-4o when the mini model's self-reported confidence or a classifier flags the task as complex.

techniques.name: Prompt Compression / Optimization
techniques.description: Trim redundant wording, remove unnecessary few-shot examples, compress context, and use concise instructions to reduce input token count without harming output quality.
techniques.example: Replace verbose multi-paragraph instructions with a tight bullet list and use LLMLingua to compress long retrieved context by 2-5x before sending it to the model.

techniques.name: Output Token Capping (max_tokens + format control)
techniques.description: Explicitly limit max_tokens and instruct the model to return concise structured output (e.g. JSON only) since output tokens are typically 3-4x more expensive than input tokens.
techniques.example: Set max_tokens=150 and add 'Respond only with valid JSON, no prose' to stop the model from generating verbose explanations you will discard.

techniques.name: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) over Long Context
techniques.description: Instead of stuffing entire documents into the prompt, retrieve only the top-k relevant chunks via vector search, drastically reducing input tokens per query.
techniques.example: Rather than passing a 50-page manual, embed it and retrieve only the 3 most relevant paragraphs to answer a support question.

techniques.name: Request Batching
techniques.description: Group multiple independent requests into a single batch API call (or batch endpoint) to amortize overhead and access discounted asynchronous batch pricing.
techniques.savings: Up to 50% reduction via batch pricing
techniques.example: Use OpenAI's Batch API for non-urgent jobs like nightly classification to get ~50% off standard token rates with a 24-hour turnaround.

techniques.name: Streaming + Early Termination
techniques.description: Stream responses and stop generation as soon as the needed content (e.g. a stop sequence or sufficient answer) is produced, avoiding paying for unneeded trailing tokens.
techniques.example: Define a stop sequence like '###END' so the model halts generation immediately after completing the structured answer.

techniques.name: Fine-tuned / Distilled Small Models
techniques.description: Distill behavior of a large model into a smaller fine-tuned model for a narrow task, so most production traffic runs on a cheaper model at inference time.
techniques.example: Fine-tune GPT-4o-mini on 1,000 GPT-4o-labeled examples to handle your classification workload at a fraction of the per-call cost.

tools.name: GPTCache
tools.description: Open-source semantic caching library for LLM queries using embedding similarity to return cached responses and cut redundant API calls.
tools.pricing_paid: Free (open-source, Apache 2.0); self-hosting infra costs only

tools.name: Redis Semantic Cache
tools.description: Vector-similarity caching built on Redis to store and retrieve LLM responses by semantic meaning, reducing token spend and latency.
tools.pricing_paid: Free open-source Redis; Redis Cloud paid tiers from ~$5/mo scaling with usage

tools.name: LiteLLM
tools.description: Unified proxy/SDK across 100+ LLM providers with built-in caching, routing, fallbacks, rate limiting, and cost tracking.
tools.pricing_paid: Free open-source; LiteLLM Enterprise custom pricing for SSO/support

tools.name: Helicone
tools.description: LLM observability and gateway platform offering request logging, cost analytics, caching, and prompt management.
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier (10k requests/mo); paid plans from ~$20/mo and usage-based

tools.name: LangChain
tools.description: LLM application framework with built-in caching (in-memory, Redis, SQLite, semantic), prompt templating, and model routing abstractions.

tools.name: LLMLingua
tools.description: Microsoft prompt-compression toolkit that compresses prompts and context up to 20x while preserving task performance.

tools.name: OpenRouter
tools.description: Unified API gateway for many model providers enabling easy model routing, fallback, and cost comparison across models.
tools.pricing_paid: Pay-as-you-go pass-through pricing with a small routing fee

tools.name: Portkey
tools.description: AI gateway with semantic caching, routing, load balancing, observability, and spend governance for production LLM apps.
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier; paid plans from ~$49/mo and enterprise pricing

quick_wins: Enable prompt caching by moving static system prompts and few-shot examples to the start of every request for up to 90% input savings on repeat calls.
Route easy queries to a cheap small model (e.g. GPT-4o-mini) and only escalate complex ones, cutting cost 50-80%.
Set max_tokens and instruct concise/JSON-only output to avoid paying for verbose unused output tokens.
Add a semantic cache (Redis/GPTCache) so paraphrased repeat questions return cached answers without an LLM call.
Trim and compress prompts/context with LLMLingua or manual editing to remove redundant tokens before sending.
